To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) The quark mass dependent spectrum of the Nambu–Goto string with heavy quark at its ends may be unstable in the infrared region.
the first excited state of a string with heavy quark masses at its ends may be arbitrarily close to the ground one.
(1) the spectrum of a string with quark-antiquark at its ends has an infrared instability, and that (2) the spectrum of the string with two quark masses is not a smooth function of the mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) How the string model with quark mass dependence is modified in comparison with the standard one?
the following problem: What is the role of the quark masses for the stability of the hadronic string with point-- like masses (quarks)?
the following problem: what is the minimal mass for the quark which is needed to make the hadronic string with quarks at its end stable?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the string model is not a good approximation for describing the quark--antiquark system for the large quark mass values.
the string model with quark masses at its ends is a very useful model for qualitative description of the hadron spectrum, but the quantitative analysis requires a modification of this model.
the string model of hadrons with point--like heavy quarks at ends is not a good approximation to real hadrons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Nambu-Goto string with point-like quarks at its end-points is an unstable system.
the string with point--masses at its ends is unstable.
we have found that the Nambu-Goto string with heavy quark masses at its ends is unstable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the case of the string with point--masses at its ends the quark mass dependence on the energy spectrum is not monotone.
the string with massive quarks at its end is not stable and the quark mass dependence is not monotonic.
the quark mass dependence is crucial for stability of string solutions.
